comment: Semantic-band probe fixture: a 28-digest journey with planted OLD facts (indexes 1-6) that a budget squeeze under oldest-first trimming always discards. Each case's action returns to one planted fact; mustRecall tokens are names/objects NOT present in the action text, so a recall hit proves the band carried the memory (not parroting). The control case ties to nothing old — it guards against ranked trimming sacrificing recency. Digests are fact-shaped (all would plausibly survive milestone selection; this fixture tests the trim layer below it).
world: A rain-worn trade coast where goods move by ferry and mule track. Small harbors, tidal marshes, and a fortified hill town inland. No magic; weather, debts, and reputations are the real forces.
playerTrait: A young trader working your late father's route for the first time, ledger in hand.
location: Harrowgate, the hill fort's market terrace
digests: You land at Sedge Ferry with your father's ledger and take his old trade route inland.
Maren the ferrywoman entrusts you with a sealed letter for her brother Callum, sworn to his hand only.
You hide your coin pouch under the loose hearthstone in your room at the Gull and Anchor inn.
A scarred drover named Weck blames you for his spilled cart and swears you will pay him by month's end.
Innkeeper Odd lends you his brass storm lantern and makes you promise to return it on your way back.
You learn the high pass is buried by rockslide; the marsh causeway is now the only road north.
You buy a gray mule at the fish market and tie a red ribbon to its halter so it cannot be swapped.
You leave the harbor at dawn and follow the levee path toward the marshes.
A peddler shares your fire and trades you dried eel for needles and thread.
Rain forces you to shelter half a day under a ruined boat hull.
You pay the causeway toll keeper two coppers and cross the first span.
A heron startles the mule; your ledger lands in the mud and dries stained but readable.
You camp on a shell mound and mend the mule's girth strap by firelight.
Two fowlers point out the safe fork where the causeway splits at the drowned willow.
You sell needles to a marsh farmwife and note the price in the ledger.
Fog holds you a morning; you inch forward lead-rope in hand.
You reach the causeway's end and climb onto firm ground below the hills.
A shepherd boy walks you an hour and talks the whole way about his dog.
You trade the dried eel for a wheel of hard cheese at a crossroads stall.
You sleep in a hay barn after helping its owner rack the last of the cut grass.
A wagon train bound for Harrowgate lets you walk in its dust for safety.
You mend a teamster's snapped rein in trade for bread and news of the fort.
You sight Harrowgate's walls at dusk and camp below the gate field.
Morning queue at the fort gate; a guard chalks your name and waves you through.
You stable the mule inside the walls and pay a boy to watch your packs.
You walk Harrowgate's market terrace, learning stall prices before you sell.
A cloth merchant named Sera offers you standing space beside her awning.
You set out your needles and thread on a borrowed board as the market fills.

cases.action: I ask the gate guard where I can find a man called Callum.

cases.action: I think back to whether my savings are safe while I am away up here.

cases.action: I spot the scarred drover from the harbor pushing through the market crowd toward me.

cases.action: I plan my route back to the harbor and what I still owe there.
